question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The rabbit was remain stationary to avoid being seen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. remained stationary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs a single finite verb in the simple past tense. "was remain" wrongly puts the bare base form (V1) "remain" after the auxiliary "was", which is grammatically impossible — after "be" we need either an -ing form (was remaining) or a past participle (V3) in the passive (was seen). Here "remain" is an intransitive linking verb, so it must simply be changed to its past form "remained".

◦ Correct: The rabbit remained stationary to avoid being seen.

• "Remain" here works as a linking (copular) verb followed by the adjective "stationary" (= not moving), exactly like "stay/keep": He remained silent / She stayed calm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("No improvement") is wrong because the printed segment "was remain stationary" is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 ("remain stationary") would give "The rabbit remain stationary", which fails subject–verb agreement — the singular subject "The rabbit" needs "remains", and the past-tense context ("to avoid being seen") demands "remained".

• Option 4 ("were remained stationary") is doubly wrong: a plural verb "were" with a singular subject, and a passive form of an intransitive verb (an intransitive verb like "remain" can never be made passive).

NOTE

• Rule for SSC: Intransitive verbs (remain, arrive, die, happen, appear, sleep, come, go) cannot be used in the passive voice.

• After forms of "be" (is/am/are/was/were), use V-ing (continuous) or V3 (passive) — never the bare V1.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Improved policing is vitally but not sufficient.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is vitally but.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the linking verb "is" we need an adjective, not an adverb, because the word describes the subject ("Improved policing"). "Vitally" is an adverb; the required adjective is "vital" (= extremely important, essential).

◦ Correct: Improved policing is vital but not sufficient.

• Parallelism also demands it: the sentence balances "vital but not sufficient" — both must be adjectives in the same form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 ("Improved policing") is correct — "improved" is a past participle used as an adjective before the gerund-noun "policing".

• Option 3 ("not sufficient.") is correct — "sufficient" is an adjective following the ellipted verb "is".

• Option 4 ("No error") is wrong because a definite adverb-for-adjective error exists in the first part.

NOTE

• Linking verbs (be, seem, appear, look, feel, taste, smell, sound, become, remain) take an adjective as complement, not an adverb: She looks beautiful (not beautifully); The soup tastes good (not well).

• Action verbs take adverbs: She sings beautifully. (महत्वपूर्ण — vital)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

In the groove
option_1: To muse on in an aimless manner
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Starting to perform very well.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in the groove" means performing very well / in top form; doing something with skill and confidence. (लय में आ जाना / बेहतरीन प्रदर्शन करना)

◦ Example: After a slow start, the batsman got in the groove and scored a century.

• The expression comes from a gramophone needle running smoothly in the groove of a record — everything flowing smoothly and rhythmically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("To muse on in an aimless manner") describes "to woolgather / daydream", not this idiom.

• Option 3 ("Simplify the producers") is not a meaning of any standard idiom.

• Option 4 ("A widely debated issue") would suit "a burning question / a moot point".

NOTE

• Related idioms of good performance: "on a roll", "in fine fettle", "on top of one's game", "hitting one's stride".

• Its opposite: "out of sorts", "off colour", "in a rut" (stuck in a dull routine).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Advantage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Boon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Advantage" (noun) means a favourable circumstance; a benefit or gain. Its closest synonym here is "boon", which means a thing that is very helpful or beneficial; a blessing. (लाभ / वरदान)

◦ Example: Cheap mobile data has been a boon/advantage for rural students.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Vital" (अत्यावश्यक) is an adjective meaning essential — it is not a noun and does not mean advantage.

• Option 3 "Unfrock" (पद से हटाना) is a verb meaning to remove a priest from office.

• Option 4 "Vengeance" (प्रतिशोध) means revenge — completely unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of advantage: benefit, gain, profit, asset, boon, edge, upper hand.

• Antonyms: disadvantage, drawback, handicap, detriment, liability.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

While persimmons can be / use in pies and tarts, you / can also enjoy them plain.
option_2: use in pies and tarts, you
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. use in pies and tarts, you.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause is in the passive voice: "persimmons can be ...". The structure modal + be + V3 (past participle) requires "used", not the base form "use".

◦ Correct: While persimmons can be used in pies and tarts, you can also enjoy them plain.

• Persimmons are the receivers of the action (someone uses them), so the passive is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("While persimmons can be") is correct — "While" introduces a contrast clause and "can be" is a proper modal + be.

• Option 4 ("can also enjoy them plain.") is correct — active voice with the object "them" and the adjective "plain" (= without any addition).

• Option 3 ("No error") is wrong because the participle error is clear.

NOTE

• Passive with modals = modal + be + V3: can be done, must be finished, should be written, may be used.

• A very common SSC trap is printing V1 instead of V3 after "be" — always check the third form.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Reluctant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inclined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reluctant" means unwilling and hesitant; disinclined to do something. (अनिच्छुक)

• Its antonym is "inclined", meaning willing, disposed or having a tendency to do something. (इच्छुक / प्रवृत्त)

◦ Example: He was reluctant to speak, but she was inclined to share everything.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Loathe" (घृणा करना) is a verb meaning to hate intensely — not an antonym of reluctant.

• Option 2 "Cagey" (सतर्क/टालमटोल करने वाला) means secretive and unwilling to give information — closer to a synonym.

• Option 4 "Abatis" is a military term for a defensive barrier of felled trees — entirely unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of reluctant: unwilling, hesitant, loath, averse, disinclined, grudging.

• Antonyms: willing, inclined, eager, keen, ready, enthusiastic.

question:
Fill in the blank with appropriate word.

His place was ________ in the team after he displayed his explosive batting style.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. cemented.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cement" as a verb means to make something firm, secure and permanent. The collocation "cement one's place / cement a position" is standard in sports writing. (स्थान पक्का करना)

◦ Correct: His place was cemented in the team after he displayed his explosive batting style.

• The clue is the positive cause — "explosive batting style" — which would strengthen, not weaken, his position.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fermented" (किण्वित) refers to sugar being chemically converted into alcohol/acid — used for food and drink, not places.

• Option 2 "affected" (प्रभावित) is vague and neutral; it does not convey the strengthening implied by good performance.

• Option 3 "belittled" (कमतर आँकना) means to make someone/something seem unimportant — the opposite of what good batting achieves.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "cement": cement a friendship, cement ties, cement a reputation, cement a legacy, cement one's place.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The cat was lastly see in the backyard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. last seen in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is in the passive voice ("The cat was ..."), so it must be followed by the past participle (V3) "seen" — see – saw – seen.

• The correct adverb is "last" (= most recently), not "lastly" (= finally, used to introduce the final point in a list).

◦ Correct: The cat was last seen in the backyard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("last saw in") uses the past simple "saw", which cannot follow "was".

• Option 2 ("No improvement") is wrong because "lastly see" is doubly incorrect.

• Option 4 ("last see in") wrongly keeps the base form after "was".

NOTE

• last (adverb) = most recently → When did you last meet him?

• lastly (adverb) = finally, in the last place → Lastly, I would like to thank my parents.

• Passive structure: be + V3 — was seen, is written, were taken, has been done.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A feeling of excitement or happiness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Exhilaration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exhilaration" is a feeling of great excitement, elation and happiness. (उल्लास / रोमांच)

◦ Example: The exhilaration of standing on the summit made every hardship worthwhile.

• Related forms: exhilarate (verb — to make someone feel very happy and excited), exhilarating (adjective).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Desolation" (उजाड़पन / गहन दुःख) means bleak emptiness or great sorrow — the opposite feeling.

• Option 3 "Passion" (जुनून) means very strong emotion or enthusiasm, but not specifically excitement plus happiness.

• Option 4 "Simulation" (अनुकरण) means an imitation of a real process — unrelated to feelings.

NOTE

• Synonyms of exhilaration: elation, euphoria, jubilation, rapture, thrill.

• Antonyms: depression, dejection, gloom, despondency, desolation.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Don't you be clever with me, boy! I want to know what you're really ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. up to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "be up to (something)" means to be doing something, especially something mischievous or secret. (कुछ शरारत/गड़बड़ करना)

◦ Correct: I want to know what you're really up to.

• The tone of the sentence — "Don't you be clever with me, boy!" — clearly shows suspicion, which is exactly the sense carried by "up to".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "on to" — "be on to someone" means to have discovered what someone is secretly doing (the speaker's side, not the boy's).

• Option 3 "in to" is not a phrasal verb here; "into" would need an object ("what you're really into" = what you enjoy), which changes the meaning entirely.

• Option 4 "up about" is not a standard English phrase.

NOTE

• Common "up" phrases: be up to (be doing something sly), be up for (be willing), be up against (face a difficulty), be fed up with (be annoyed by).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

It is believed that difficult tasks demand lot of our resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. difficult tasks demand lot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The quantifier "lot" is a countable noun and can never stand alone — it always takes the article "a": "a lot of".

◦ Correct: It is believed that difficult tasks demand a lot of our resources.

• "A lot of" means "a large quantity of" and can be used with both countable and uncountable nouns.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("It is believed that") is correct — a standard impersonal passive opening.

• Option 4 ("of our resources.") is correct — the preposition "of" properly follows "a lot".

• Option 2 ("No error") is wrong because the missing article is a clear mistake.

NOTE

• Article rules with quantifiers: a lot of, a great deal of, a number of, a couple of, a few, a little — the article is compulsory.

• Note the difference: a lot of (much/many) vs lots of (informal, same meaning) — but never bare "lot of".

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The first time that nuclear radiation has been washed off with a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. quick shower.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A quick shower" is the fixed natural collocation in English for a short bath under running water. (झटपट स्नान)

◦ Correct: ... nuclear radiation has been washed off with a quick shower.

• Although "fast" and "speedy" also mean rapid, English usage pairs "quick" with shower/bath/wash/bite/word/look, not "fast" or "speedy".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fast shower" — "fast" describes speed of movement (a fast car, a fast bowler), not the brief duration of an activity.

• Option 3 "speedy shower" — "speedy" collocates with recovery, delivery, response, trial, not shower.

• Option 4 "energetic shower" — "energetic" describes a person full of energy, which is meaningless with "shower".

NOTE

• Collocation is a high-scoring SSC area. Learn: quick shower/nap/bite/glance; fast car/train/food; speedy recovery/trial; rapid growth/progress; swift action/response.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The necessity of resisting the ________ demands of the prophets led to the introduction of new rules for distinguishing true and false prophets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. relentless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Relentless" means never stopping; continuing without any let-up or mercy; persistent. (निरंतर / अथक)

◦ Correct: The necessity of resisting the relentless demands of the prophets ...

• The sentence says the demands had to be resisted and new rules had to be framed — this implies constant, unyielding pressure, which "relentless" captures exactly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "unimpeachable" (निर्दोष / प्रश्नातीत) means beyond doubt or reproach — demands that cannot be questioned would not need to be resisted.

• Option 3 "irreparable" (अपूरणीय) means impossible to repair; it describes damage or loss, never demands.

• Option 4 "imperturbable" (अविचल / शांतचित्त) means calm and not easily upset — it describes a person's temperament, not demands.

NOTE

• Synonyms of relentless: unrelenting, persistent, incessant, unremitting, implacable, ceaseless.

• Antonyms: intermittent, occasional, merciful, yielding.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Connivance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Connivance" — CON + NIV + ANCE. It means willingness to allow or secretly help in a wrongdoing; secret cooperation in a wrong act. (मिलीभगत / दुरभिसंधि)

◦ Example: The scam was carried out with the connivance of senior officials.

• Memory key: it comes from the verb "connive" (to conspire / to turn a blind eye) + the noun suffix "-ance" → connive – connivance (the final "e" of connive is dropped).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Connievence" wrongly inserts an extra "e" and uses "-ence".

• Option 2 "Conniavance" wrongly inserts an extra "a".

• Option 4 "Conivance" wrongly uses a single "n" — the word has a double "n".

NOTE

• Words with the same "-ance" pattern from verbs ending in "-e": observe → observance, endure → endurance, insure → insurance, contrive → contrivance.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Difficult to interpret or understand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enigmatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enigmatic" means mysterious, puzzling and difficult to interpret or understand. (रहस्यमय / पहेली जैसा)

◦ Example: The Mona Lisa is famous for her enigmatic smile.

• It derives from "enigma" = a riddle or a puzzling person/thing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Explicable" (व्याख्या योग्य) means able to be explained — the exact opposite of the given definition.

• Option 2 "Emulate" (अनुकरण करना) is a verb meaning to imitate someone in order to match or surpass them.

• Option 4 "Endemic" (स्थानिक) means regularly found in a particular place or among a particular group (an endemic disease/species).

NOTE

• Synonyms of enigmatic: mysterious, cryptic, inscrutable, baffling, obscure, arcane.

• Antonyms: clear, obvious, explicable, straightforward, transparent.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

Any book on any subject risks irrelevance or smallness compared to this (behemoth).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Midget.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "behemoth" is something enormous and immensely powerful — a huge creature, organisation or thing. (विशालकाय)

• Its antonym is "midget", meaning something extremely small; a tiny version of something. (बहुत छोटा / लघु)

◦ Example: Beside that industrial behemoth, our workshop looks like a midget.

• The word "behemoth" comes from the enormous beast described in the Book of Job in the Bible.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Monster" (राक्षस / विशाल वस्तु) is a synonym of behemoth in the sense of hugeness.

• Option 2 "Colossus" (विशाल मूर्ति / विशालकाय) also means a gigantic thing — again a synonym (from the Colossus of Rhodes).

• Option 3 "Dreadnought" was a class of huge battleship, so it too suggests great size and power.

NOTE

• Synonyms of behemoth: giant, colossus, mammoth, titan, leviathan, juggernaut.

• Antonyms: midget, dwarf, pygmy, miniature, mite.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

I think I might take (French leave) this afternoon and go to the cinema.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Absence without permission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to take French leave" means to be absent from work or a place without permission or without informing anyone. (बिना अनुमति के अनुपस्थित रहना)

◦ Example: Three clerks took French leave on the day of the match.

• The sentence supports this — the speaker plans to slip away "this afternoon and go to the cinema" instead of working.

• Origin: an 18th-century French social custom of leaving a party without saying goodbye to the host.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("To try hard") matches idioms like "go all out" / "leave no stone unturned".

• Option 3 ("To be inconsistent") matches "blow hot and cold".

• Option 4 ("To have a slight encounter") matches "a brush with (something)".

NOTE

• Other "French" expressions: French window (a full-length glazed door), excuse my French (apology for swearing).

• Similar idioms of absconding: "give someone the slip", "do a bunk", "play truant".

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: They superseded the old statute with a new one.
option_2: They will be celebrating their twelth anniversary this April.
option_3: He had no sense of rhythme whatsoever.
option_4: I wrote her a reciept for the money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They superseded the old statute with a new one.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 1 is spelt correctly:

◦ "superseded" (SUPER + SEDE + D) — note the unusual "-sede" ending; it means replaced / took the place of. (प्रतिस्थापित किया)

◦ "statute" (STAT + UTE) — a written law passed by a legislature. (क़ानून / अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 misspells "twelth"; the correct spelling is "twelfth" (twelve → twelfth, keeping the "f").

• Option 3 misspells "rhythme"; the correct spelling is "rhythm" — no final "e" (RHY + THM).

• Option 4 misspells "reciept"; the correct spelling is "receipt" — "ei" after "c", with a silent "p".

NOTE

• "Supersede" is the only common English word ending in -sede. Words ending in -ceed: exceed, proceed, succeed; all the rest take -cede: precede, concede, recede, intercede.

• Spelling rule: "i before e except after c" — receipt, deceive, perceive, ceiling.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

From start to finish, the treatment of the defendants was a (travesty) of legal due process.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. mockery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "travesty" is an absurd, distorted or debased imitation of something — something that makes a serious thing look ridiculous. (उपहास / विकृत नक़ल)

• Its closest synonym is "mockery", especially in the fixed phrases "a travesty of justice" and "a mockery of justice".

◦ Correct: ... the treatment of the defendants was a mockery of legal due process.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "magic" (जादू) has no connection with a distorted imitation.

• Option 3 "tribute" (श्रद्धांजलि / प्रशंसा) means an act showing respect or admiration — the opposite in tone.

• Option 4 "slurry" (कीचड़ जैसा घोल) is a semi-liquid mixture of water with cement, mud or manure — a technical noun, not related.

NOTE

• Synonyms of travesty: mockery, parody, caricature, farce, distortion, sham.

• "Due process" is the legal principle that a person must be given fair treatment through the normal judicial system.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

He had to brake suddenly to avoiding hitting the deer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. avoid hitting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The infinitive of purpose "to" must be followed by the bare base form (V1) of the verb — "to avoid", never "to avoiding" or "to avoided".

• The verb "avoid" is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), so "avoid hitting" is correct.

◦ Correct: He had to brake suddenly to avoid hitting the deer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("No improvement") is wrong — "to avoiding" is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 ("avoided hitting") wrongly puts a past-tense verb after "to".

• Option 3 ("avoided hits") is wrong on both counts — past tense after "to", and a noun instead of a gerund.

NOTE

• Verbs always followed by the gerund (V-ing): avoid, enjoy, mind, finish, suggest, admit, deny, consider, practise, risk, postpone.

• Verbs followed by the to-infinitive: want, hope, decide, agree, refuse, promise, manage, plan.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Pumpkins contain high levels of (1) ______. These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals, a (2) ______ of unstable molecule that can sometimes (3) ______ damage to our cells, which may cause ageing and contribute to (4)______ diseases over time. While some antioxidants occur (5) ______ in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. antioxidants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The very next sentence defines the blank: "These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals" — that is the textbook definition of "antioxidants". (प्रतिऑक्सीकारक)

• The last line of the passage confirms it: "While some antioxidants occur ... in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables."

◦ Correct: Pumpkins contain high levels of antioxidants.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sentiments" (भावनाएँ) means feelings — a pumpkin cannot contain them.

• Option 2 "atoms" is far too general; every substance is made of atoms, and atoms do not "fight free radicals".

• Option 4 "supplements" are extra doses taken in addition to the diet, not something naturally present inside a vegetable.

NOTE

• Contextual clue technique: when a blank is immediately followed by "These are ...", the definition that follows tells you exactly what the blank must be.

• Common dietary antioxidants: Vitamin C, Vitamin E, beta-carotene, lycopene, selenium.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Pumpkins contain high levels of (1) ______. These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals, a (2) ______ of unstable molecule that can sometimes (3) ______ damage to our cells, which may cause ageing and contribute to (4)______ diseases over time. While some antioxidants occur (5) ______ in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. type.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase needed is "a type of unstable molecule" — "type of" means a kind/category of, and free radicals are indeed a kind of unstable molecule. (एक प्रकार का)

◦ Correct: ... free radicals, a type of unstable molecule that can sometimes ...

• The structure "a ______ of + noun" here demands a classifying noun, and "type" is the natural choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "pattern" (प्रतिरूप) refers to a repeated design or arrangement — a single molecule is not a pattern.

• Option 2 "subject" (विषय) means a topic of study or the grammatical subject — meaningless here.

• Option 4 "term" (शब्द / पद) refers to a word or expression; free radicals are the molecules themselves, not merely a word.

NOTE

• Classifying nouns used in this pattern: a type of, a kind of, a sort of, a form of, a variety of, a class of, a category of.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Pumpkins contain high levels of (1) ______. These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals, a (2) ______ of unstable molecule that can sometimes (3) ______ damage to our cells, which may cause ageing and contribute to (4)______ diseases over time. While some antioxidants occur (5) ______ in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. cause.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "cause damage" — to bring about or produce harm. (नुकसान पहुँचाना)

◦ Correct: ... unstable molecule that can sometimes cause damage to our cells ...

• The modal "can" is followed by the base form (V1) "cause", which fits the grammar as well as the meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "treats" (उपचार करना) means to cure — the opposite of causing harm; it is also a wrong form after "can".

• Option 2 "plan" (योजना बनाना) requires intention, which a molecule cannot have.

• Option 3 "fall" (गिरना) is intransitive and cannot take the object "damage".

NOTE

• Verbs that collocate with "damage": cause damage, do damage, inflict damage, suffer damage, repair damage.

• After modals (can, may, must, should, will), always use the bare infinitive (V1).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Pumpkins contain high levels of (1) ______. These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals, a (2) ______ of unstable molecule that can sometimes (3) ______ damage to our cells, which may cause ageing and contribute to (4)______ diseases over time. While some antioxidants occur (5) ______ in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. various.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective before the plural noun "diseases". "Various" means several different; of many kinds, which fits the general statement that free-radical damage contributes to many different diseases. (विभिन्न / अनेक प्रकार के)

◦ Correct: ... which may cause ageing and contribute to various diseases over time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spotted" (चित्तीदार) means marked with spots — it describes appearance, not diseases in general.

• Option 3 "neutral" (तटस्थ) means impartial or chemically neither acidic nor basic; "neutral diseases" is meaningless.

• Option 4 "references" (संदर्भ) is a noun, so it cannot modify "diseases" in this position.

NOTE

• Similar quantity adjectives: various, several, numerous, sundry, diverse, assorted — all take a plural noun.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Pumpkins contain high levels of (1) ______. These are molecules that fight harmful free radicals, a (2) ______ of unstable molecule that can sometimes (3) ______ damage to our cells, which may cause ageing and contribute to (4)______ diseases over time. While some antioxidants occur (5) ______ in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. naturally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts antioxidants produced inside the body with those obtained from fruits and vegetables. The phrase "occur naturally" means to exist or be produced by nature, without artificial help. (प्राकृतिक रूप से)

◦ Correct: While some antioxidants occur naturally in our bodies, others we get from fruits and vegetables.

• The word "While" signals a contrast, and "naturally (in our bodies)" vs "from outside sources" completes that contrast perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "casually" (लापरवाही से / अनौपचारिक रूप से) means without much care or attention — biological processes are not "casual".

• Option 3 "systematically" (व्यवस्थित रूप से) implies a planned method, which does not suit a spontaneous bodily process.

• Option 4 "informally" (अनौपचारिक रूप से) relates to manner and style of behaviour, not to biological occurrence.

NOTE

• "Occur naturally" is a standard science collocation: Fluoride occurs naturally in groundwater.

• Related: naturally occurring (adjective) — naturally occurring minerals, naturally occurring antioxidants.

question: Mallika Sarabhai received the prestigious ______ award by Government of India in the year 2010.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Bhushan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The eminent Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, actress and activist Mallika Sarabhai was conferred the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India in 2010. (मल्लिका साराभाई — पद्म भूषण, 2010)

• She is the daughter of the space scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and the classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai, and heads the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Padma Awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and are given in three grades:

◦ Padma Vibhushan — for exceptional and distinguished service (2nd highest civilian award).

◦ Padma Bhushan — for distinguished service of a high order (3rd highest).

◦ Padma Shri — for distinguished service (4th highest).

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954.

NOTE

• The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour, instituted in 1961 and first given to G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam) in 1965.

• Mallika Sarabhai also received the Padma Bhushan for Arts, and is known for her role as Draupadi in Peter Brook's The Mahabharata.

question: In West Bengal, localised thunderstorms are known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kaal Baisakhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In West Bengal, the violent localised evening thunderstorms of the pre-monsoon season (April–May) are called "Kaal Baisakhi" (literally "the calamity of the month of Baisakh"). (काल बैसाखी)

• These are also known as "Nor'westers" because they usually approach from the north-west, bringing strong squalls, lightning and short spells of very heavy rain.

• They are useful for jute, tea and rice cultivation in Bengal and Assam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Loo — a hot, dry and dusty wind blowing over the northern plains of India in May–June; it can cause heat-stroke.

• Chinook — a warm, dry local wind on the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains in North America ("snow-eater").

• Mango showers — pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka that help mangoes ripen; in Karnataka they are also called "blossom showers" as they help coffee flowers bloom.

NOTE

• Other local names for Nor'westers: "Bardoichila" in Assam, and "Kaal Baisakhi" in West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar.

question: Pandit Kishan Maharaj was a famous Indian ______ player.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Kishan Maharaj (1923–2008) was one of India's greatest tabla maestros, belonging to the Benaras gharana. (पं. किशन महाराज — तबला)

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1973) and the Padma Vibhushan (2002).

• He accompanied legends such as Pt. Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan and Pt. Bhimsen Joshi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The tabla is a pair of membranophone (percussion) drums — the smaller right-hand dayan/tabla and the larger left-hand bayan/dagga.

• Other famous tabla players: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pt. Samta Prasad, Pt. Anindo Chatterjee, Ustad Ahmed Jan Thirakwa.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs frequently asked in SSC: Sitar – Pt. Ravi Shankar; Sarangi – Pt. Ram Narayan; Flute – Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia; Shehnai – Ustad Bismillah Khan; Santoor – Pt. Shivkumar Sharma; Sarod – Ustad Amjad Ali Khan.

question: Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India (1899–1905), announced the Partition of Bengal in July 1905, which came into effect on 16 October 1905. (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905)

• The official reason given was administrative convenience, but the real motive was to divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal — a policy of "divide and rule".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The partition triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement (1905), in which foreign goods were burnt and Indian goods promoted. Rabindranath Tagore composed "Amar Sonar Bangla" and 16 October was observed as Raksha Bandhan Day to show Hindu-Muslim unity.

• The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge II, when the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

NOTE

• Other acts of Curzon: the Indian Universities Act (1904), the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904), and the creation of the Archaeological Survey of India's modern framework and the North-West Frontier Province (1901).

question: The process of depositing a layer of zinc on iron is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is galvanisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Galvanisation" is the process of depositing a protective layer of zinc on iron or steel to prevent rusting (corrosion). (जस्तीकरण / गैल्वनीकरण)

• Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes first and acts as a sacrificial coating, protecting the iron underneath even if the layer is scratched.

• Common methods: hot-dip galvanising (dipping in molten zinc) and electro-galvanising (electroplating).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Filtration — separating an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter.

• Sedimentation — allowing heavier insoluble particles to settle at the bottom of a liquid.

• Crystallisation — obtaining pure crystals of a solid from its solution by evaporation and cooling.

NOTE

• Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide — Fe₂O₃·xH₂O; both oxygen and moisture are needed for rusting.

• Other anti-corrosion methods: painting, greasing, oiling, tinning, chrome-plating, anodising and using alloys such as stainless steel (iron + chromium + nickel).

question: Prithviraja III defeated Afghan ruler sultan Muhammad Ghori in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1191.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prithviraj Chauhan III defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, fought near Thanesar (present-day Haryana). (तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध — 1191)

• Ghori was wounded and forced to retreat, but he returned the very next year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori defeated and killed Prithviraj Chauhan. This battle is regarded as a turning point in Indian history, as it laid the foundation of Muslim rule in northern India.

• Ghori's general and slave, Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty in 1206, the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

NOTE

• Prithviraj Chauhan was the last great ruler of the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty of Ajmer and Delhi. His court poet Chand Bardai wrote the epic "Prithviraj Raso".

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main parts of cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vacuole.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three basic/main parts of a cell are the cell membrane (plasma membrane), the cytoplasm and the nucleus. (कोशिका के तीन मुख्य भाग)

• A "vacuole" is only one of the several cell organelles present inside the cytoplasm — it is not counted among the three fundamental parts. (रसधानी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Cell membrane — a selectively permeable covering that controls the entry and exit of substances.

• Cytoplasm — the jelly-like fluid between the membrane and the nucleus, containing all the organelles.

• Nucleus — the control centre of the cell, containing chromosomes (DNA); discovered by Robert Brown (1831).

• Vacuoles store water, food and wastes; plant cells have one large central vacuole that provides turgidity and rigidity.

NOTE

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke (1665) in a cork slice. Cell theory was given by Schleiden and Schwann (1838–39) and completed by Rudolf Virchow (1855) with "Omnis cellula-e cellula" (all cells arise from pre-existing cells).

question: Part IV of the Indian constitution provides for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Directive Principles of State policy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). (नीति निदेशक तत्व)

• They are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court of law) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37), and the State has a duty to apply them while making laws.

• They were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which in turn took the idea from Spain.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Part III (Articles 12–35) — Fundamental Rights (borrowed from the USA).

• Part IVA (Article 51A) — Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee (borrowed from the erstwhile USSR).

• Part V (Articles 52–151) — the Union, which includes the Union Executive (President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, Attorney General).

NOTE

• Important DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), Article 45 (early childhood care), Article 48A (protection of environment), Article 50 (separation of judiciary from executive).

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognised stroke of a swimming competition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leg stroke.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Leg stroke" is not a recognised swimming stroke in competitive swimming. (लेग स्ट्रोक — तैराकी की कोई मान्य शैली नहीं)

• The four official competitive strokes recognised by World Aquatics (formerly FINA) are:

◦ Freestyle (front crawl)

◦ Backstroke

◦ Breaststroke

◦ Butterfly

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Individual Medley (IM) uses all four strokes in this order — butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, freestyle.

• In the medley relay, the order is backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle.

• Swimming events are held in 50 m (long course) and 25 m (short course) pools; the Olympic pool has 10 lanes (8 used for racing).

NOTE

• Swimming has been part of the modern Olympic Games since 1896 (Athens).

• Michael Phelps (USA) is the most decorated Olympian ever with 28 medals (23 gold).

question: What was the capital of Vajji Mahajanapada?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vaishali" (in present-day Bihar) was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) Mahajanapada. (वज्जि महाजनपद की राजधानी — वैशाली)

• Vajji was a confederacy (gana-sangha) of eight clans, the most powerful being the Licchavis, and it is often described as one of the world's earliest republics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Important Mahajanapadas and their capitals: Magadha – Girivraja/Rajgir then Pataliputra; Kosala – Shravasti; Vatsa – Kaushambi; Avanti – Ujjain/Mahishmati; Kuru – Indraprastha (Hastinapura); Panchala – Ahichchhatra/Kampilya; Gandhara – Taxila; Anga – Champa.

• The 16 Mahajanapadas flourished in the 6th century BCE; they are listed in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain text Bhagavati Sutra.

NOTE

• Vaishali is closely linked with Lord Mahavira (born nearby at Kundagrama) and with Buddhism — the Second Buddhist Council was held here around 383 BCE during the reign of Kalashoka.

question: Nati is a folk dance of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nati" is the most popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, especially of the Kullu, Sirmaur, Shimla and Kinnaur regions. (नाटी — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

• It is performed in a circular/serpentine formation to the beat of instruments such as the dhol, nagara, shehnai, karnal and narsingha.

• The "Kullvi Nati" entered the Guinness World Records in 2015 as the largest folk dance performed by around 9,892 women at Kullu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Himachal Pradesh: Kinnauri Nati, Namgen, Losar Shona Chuksam, Chham, Dangi, Jhoori.

• Madhya Pradesh — Matki, Grida, Phulpati, Karma, Tertali.

• Arunachal Pradesh — Bardo Chham, Ponung, Wancho, Popir.

• Andhra Pradesh — Kuchipudi (classical), Butta Bommalu, Veeranatyam, Dhimsa.

NOTE

• Folk dances are a high-frequency SSC topic. Learn: Bihu – Assam; Garba – Gujarat; Bhangra – Punjab; Ghoomar – Rajasthan; Lavani – Maharashtra; Chhau – Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal; Bihu – Assam; Rouf – Jammu & Kashmir.

question: Under 'SAMRIDDHI 2022-23 (Strengthening & Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development in Delhi)', people will be able to pay only the principal amount of the current and pending tax of past _______ years for residential properties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the SAMRIDDHI 2022-23 scheme (Strengthening and Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development in Delhi), residential property owners could pay only the principal amount of the current and the previous five years' property tax, with all interest and penalty waived. (पिछले पाँच वर्ष)

• For non-residential (commercial) properties, the relief covered the current year plus the previous six years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) as a one-time property-tax amnesty scheme to boost revenue and widen the tax base.

• The three municipal corporations of Delhi (North, South and East) were re-unified into a single MCD in May 2022.

NOTE

• Property tax is a major source of revenue for urban local bodies (ULBs). The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to municipalities and added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) to the Constitution.

question: Organisms that take in the food synthesised by plants are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heterotrophs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heterotrophs" are organisms that cannot make their own food and therefore depend on food synthesised by plants (or other organisms). (विषमपोषी)

◦ Examples: all animals, fungi and most bacteria; human beings are heterotrophs.

• The word comes from Greek: hetero (other) + trophe (nutrition).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Autotrophs (स्वपोषी) prepare their own food, usually through photosynthesis — green plants, algae and cyanobacteria.

• Saprophytes (मृतजीवी) obtain nutrition from dead and decaying organic matter — e.g. mushroom, bread mould (Rhizopus), yeast.

• Parasites (परजीवी) live on or inside a host and take food from it — e.g. Cuscuta (amarbel), tapeworm, lice.

NOTE

• Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

• In a food chain, autotrophs = producers and heterotrophs = consumers/decomposers.

question: “Agricultural Census” is conducted in India at an interval of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Agriculture Census in India is conducted every five years (quinquennially) by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. (कृषि गणना — प्रत्येक पाँच वर्ष)

• It collects data on the number and area of operational holdings, their size-class distribution, tenancy, land use and cropping pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first Agriculture Census in India was conducted in 1970-71. The latest available round is the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22).

• As per the Agriculture Census 2015-16, the average size of operational holdings fell to about 1.08 hectares, and small and marginal holdings (below 2 ha) made up about 86% of all holdings.

NOTE

• The Population Census of India is decennial (every 10 years) — the first complete census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the 2011 Census was the 15th.

• The Livestock Census is also conducted every five years; the 20th Livestock Census was released in 2019.

question: The forces which work on the surface of the earth are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is exogenic forces.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exogenic (exogenetic) forces" are the forces that operate on or very near the surface of the earth, deriving their energy mainly from the sun (and gravity). (बहिर्जात बल)

• They cause weathering, erosion, transportation and deposition through agents such as running water, wind, glaciers, waves and groundwater.

• Their overall effect is denudation — they wear down the relief and level the surface, so they are called destructive forces.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Endogenic forces" act inside the earth and derive energy from the earth's internal heat (radioactivity, primordial heat). They are of two types:

◦ Diastrophic/slow forces — epeirogenic (continent-building, vertical) and orogenic (mountain-building, horizontal).

◦ Sudden forces — earthquakes and volcanoes.

• Endogenic forces are constructive — they build up relief features such as mountains, plateaus and rift valleys.

NOTE

• The interplay of endogenic (building up) and exogenic (wearing down) forces is called gradation, comprising degradation (erosion) and aggradation (deposition).

question: In which of the following decades, there was a negative growth rate in Indian population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1911 – 1921.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The decade 1911–1921 is the only decade in India's census history to record a negative population growth rate (about –0.31%). (ऋणात्मक वृद्धि दर वाला दशक)

• The main causes were the devastating influenza (Spanish flu) pandemic of 1918–19, which killed an estimated 12–17 million Indians, along with famines, epidemics (plague, cholera) and poor medical facilities.

• Because of this, 1911–1921 is called the period of "stagnant population".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Phases of India's population growth (as per Census classification):

◦ 1901–1921 — Stagnant population (high birth rate, high death rate).

◦ 1921–1951 — Steady growth; 1921 is called the "Great Divide" or demographic divide year, after which population began rising continuously.

◦ 1951–1981 — Rapid, high growth (population explosion).

◦ 1981–2011 — High growth with a definite slowdown.

NOTE

• As per Census 2011, India's population was 121.09 crore, with a decadal growth rate of 17.7%, a sex ratio of 943 and a literacy rate of 74.04%.

question: Which among the following Acts established the dual system of control by the British government and the East India Company in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pitt's India Act, 1784.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pitt's India Act of 1784 (named after the British PM William Pitt the Younger) established a system of double/dual government in India. (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट, 1784 — द्वैध शासन)

◦ It created a Board of Control to supervise political, military and revenue affairs, representing the British Government.

◦ The Court of Directors of the East India Company was left in charge of commercial affairs.

• For the first time, the Company's Indian possessions were called the "British possessions in India" and the British Government was given direct control over Indian administration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Regulating Act, 1773 — the first step by the British Parliament to control the Company; made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings was the first) and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

• Charter Act, 1813 — ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and trade with China; allowed Christian missionaries; provided ₹1 lakh a year for education.

• Charter Act, 1833 — made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck first); ended the Company's commercial functions.

• Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — introduced dyarchy in the provinces (transferred and reserved subjects) and bicameralism at the Centre.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the two "duals": Pitt's India Act, 1784 → dual government at the level of control (Board of Control + Court of Directors); GoI Act, 1919 → dyarchy in provincial administration.

question: National Waterway 2 (NW 2) is the Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of the ______ river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Waterway 2 (NW-2) is the Sadiya–Dhubri stretch of the River Brahmaputra, in Assam, with a length of about 891 km. It was declared a National Waterway in 1988. (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग-2 — ब्रह्मपुत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NW-1 — Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river system, Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia, about 1,620 km — India's longest national waterway (declared 1986).

• NW-3 — West Coast Canal (Kottapuram–Kollam) with the Champakara and Udyogmandal canals in Kerala, about 205 km (declared 1993) — India's first waterway with 24-hour navigation facility.

• NW-4 — Krishna–Godavari rivers with the Kakinada–Puducherry canals; NW-5 — Brahmani–Mahanadi delta rivers with the East Coast Canal.

• The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 national waterways. The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) was set up in 1986.

NOTE

• The Brahmaputra rises as the Tsangpo in Tibet (Chemayungdung glacier near Mansarovar), enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang/Dihang, and becomes the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

• Majuli (Assam), on the Brahmaputra, is one of the largest river islands in the world.

question: In Badminton, the length and width of the doubles court shall be of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13.40 m × 6.10 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A standard badminton court for doubles measures 13.40 m in length and 6.10 m in width. (बैडमिंटन डबल्स कोर्ट — 13.40 मी × 6.10 मी)

• For singles, the length remains 13.40 m but the width is reduced to 5.18 m (the side tramlines are excluded).

• The net height is 1.55 m at the posts and 1.524 m at the centre.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A shuttlecock weighs 4.74 – 5.50 g and has 16 feathers.

• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF), headquartered at Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. In India it is governed by the Badminton Association of India (BAI).

• Major tournaments: Thomas Cup (men's team), Uber Cup (women's team), Sudirman Cup (mixed team), All England Open.

NOTE

• Indian achievements: P. V. Sindhu — Olympic silver (2016) and bronze (2021), World Champion (2019); Saina Nehwal — Olympic bronze (2012); India won the Thomas Cup in 2022 for the first time.

• Badminton terms: smash, drop shot, lob, deuce, let, love-all, rally, shuttle.

question: Shinzo Abe, who recently died, served as Prime Minister of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Japan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shinzo Abe (1954–2022) was the Prime Minister of Japan and the longest-serving PM in Japanese history (2006–07 and again 2012–2020). (शिंजो आबे — जापान)

• He was assassinated in July 2022 while campaigning in Nara, Japan.

• He was awarded India's Padma Vibhushan in 2021 for his contribution to strengthening India–Japan relations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Abe's economic policy was popularly called "Abenomics", built on three arrows — monetary easing, fiscal stimulus and structural reforms.

• He was a key architect of the Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) comprising India, USA, Japan and Australia, and of the Indo-Pacific vision.

• Japan: capital Tokyo; currency Yen; called the "Land of the Rising Sun"; parliament is the Diet.

NOTE

• The Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train project, using Japanese Shinkansen technology, was launched during Abe's tenure with Japanese assistance.

question: Which among the famous novels is written by Indian author R. K. Narayan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The dark room.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Dark Room" (1938) is a novel by the celebrated Indian English writer R. K. Narayan (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami, 1906–2001). (आर. के. नारायण)

• Most of his works are set in the fictional South Indian town of "Malgudi".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other works of R. K. Narayan: Swami and Friends (1935), The Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher, The Financial Expert, Waiting for the Mahatma, The Guide (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1958), The Man-Eater of Malgudi, The Vendor of Sweets, Malgudi Days.

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1964) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000), and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• A Suitable Boy — Vikram Seth; Unaccustomed Earth — Jhumpa Lahiri; Half Girlfriend — Chetan Bhagat.

• R. K. Narayan's brother R. K. Laxman was the famous cartoonist who created "The Common Man".

question: The festival of Navroz or nowroj is celebrated as new year of which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parsi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Navroz (Nowruz)" literally means "new day" in Persian and is celebrated as the New Year of the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community. (नवरोज़ — पारसी नववर्ष)

• In Iran and Central Asia it is observed on the spring equinox (around 21 March); in India, the Parsis following the Shahenshahi calendar celebrate it in August, when it is also called "Pateti"-linked Navroz.

• UNESCO has inscribed Nowruz on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Parsis are followers of Zoroastrianism, founded by the prophet Zarathustra (Zoroaster); their holy book is the "Zend Avesta" and their place of worship is the Fire Temple (Agiary).

• They migrated from Persia (Iran) to India around the 8th–10th century CE, settling mainly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

NOTE

• New Year festivals of India: Ugadi (Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Baisakhi (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Cheti Chand (Sindhi), Losar (Tibetan/Buddhist).

question: In national income accounting, GVA stands for _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross value added.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In national income accounting, GVA stands for "Gross Value Added". (सकल मूल्य वर्धित)

• It measures the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption — i.e., the contribution of each producer, industry or sector to the economy.

• Relationship with GDP: GDP = GVA + Product Taxes – Product Subsidies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) — the market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a year.

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).

• NDP = GDP – Depreciation; NNP = GNP – Depreciation; NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• India shifted to measuring economic activity primarily by GVA at basic prices with the base-year revision to 2011-12 (announced in 2015).

NOTE

• National income estimates in India are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• The first scientific estimate of national income in India was made by Dr. V. K. R. V. Rao; Dadabhai Naoroji made the first attempt in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".

question: The Brihadeshwara temple at Tanjore was built by _______ rulers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brihadeeswarar (Brihadeshwara) Temple at Thanjavur (Tanjore), Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja Chola I in about 1010 CE. It is also called the "Rajarajeswaram" or the "Big Temple". (बृहदेश्वर मंदिर — चोल शासक)

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, with one of the tallest vimanas (about 66 m) in the world, topped by a massive single granite capstone.

• It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Great Living Chola Temples", along with the temples at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chandella rulers built the Khajuraho group of temples (Madhya Pradesh) — e.g., the Kandariya Mahadeva temple.

• Pallava rulers built the Shore Temple and the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram.

• Solanki (Chaulukya) rulers built the Sun Temple at Modhera and the Dilwara Jain temples patronage in Gujarat/Rajasthan.

NOTE

• The Cholas (9th–13th century CE) were famous for their naval power, local self-government through village assemblies (Ur, Sabha, Nagaram) — described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I — and for Chola bronze sculptures, especially the Nataraja.
